Adversarial review of the four flagged risk areas found no defect. (1) mergeStable: tie-break correctly favors the lowest-indexed source because the inner loop scans i in increasing order and only replaces pick on a strict isBefore (ties never displace the incumbent) - matches AC-A3's tie-break rule, confirmed against test/day-groups.test.ts's explicit tie-break test asserting both orderings. The pick===-1 break is genuinely unreachable while merged.length<total (by construction, at least one stream has a defined candidate whenever items remain), so it is defensive-and-documented, not bug-hiding. The non-null assertions on streams[pick] and cursors[pick] are safe: pick is only ever set to a valid index by the same loop that reads streams[i], and cursors is initialized to 0 for every index and only incremented for a validly-selected pick. (2) isBefore's dueDate===null guard IS reachable: bucketOf checks closed before dueDate, so the closed bucket can legitimately mix null and non-null dueDate items (mirroring pre-existing groupTasks behavior, which never date-sorted the closed bucket); returning false for a null comparison correctly falls back to source-order tie-break rather than producing wrong chronological order. Dated buckets never contain a null-dueDate item by construction of bucketOf, so the guard is dead-but-harmless there and load-bearing in the closed bucket - not a defect. (3) unwrap's filter(item.source==='task').map(item.task) type-checks for the RIGHT reason: TypeScript 6.0.3 (this project's pinned version) implements TS 5.5's inferred type-predicate narrowing for Array.prototype.filter, so the callback is automatically inferred as item is TaskDayItem and the following .map access is legal; verified empirically by an isolated repro plus npx tsc -b --force on the real tree, both zero errors. It can only silently drop an item if a caller ever fed collectDayItems a non-task source through groupTasks, which the module's own structure makes impossible today (docstring correctly calls this safe by construction); flagged as a low-severity advisory only, not blocking. (4) TodayScreen.tsx's case google: return assertNeverDaySource(item.source as never) is legitimate: the as never cast is required there only because google is still a live case, and it is the SEPARATE default: return assertNeverDaySource(item) branch (no cast) that supplies the real compile-time guarantee. Verified empirically with an isolated repro extending DaySource with a third member and mirroring TodayScreen's exact switch shape: npx tsc --noEmit --strict on the repro fails with 'Argument of type LocalItem is not assignable to parameter of type never' at the default branch, confirming the plan's load-bearing claim that adding a third DaySource member is a genuine compile error
